about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Baked Vegetable Samosas
recipes.summary: Crisp baked pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas, easy to make ahead for a snack plate.
steps: Rub the flour, salt and 2 tbsp of the oil together, then add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.

Boil the potato for 10 minutes until tender, drain well and roughly mash. Fry the onion and cumin seeds in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder, potato, peas and lemon juice, then cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each into a 22cm round, then halve each to make 8 half-moons.
Shape each half into a cone, fill with 2 tbsp of the filling and press the edges closed with a little water.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool for 5 minutes before eating.

recipes.title: Mushroom Arancini
recipes.summary: Golden crumbed risotto balls with a melting mozzarella centre, baked rather than deep-fried.
steps: Fry the mushrooms in the olive oil for 6 minutes until dry and golden, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add the stock a cup at a time, stirring, for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and creamy. Stir through the parmesan and spread on a tray to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Wrap about 2 tbsp of rice around each mozzarella cube to make 12 balls.
Roll each ball in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and hot through the middle.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian-style cheese not specified, so it is not tagged vegetarian. Per serving: 3 balls.
Food safety: the egg coating is cooked through in the oven; wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Onion Pakoras
recipes.summary: Crunchy chickpea-flour fritters packed with onion and spice, shallow-fried and best eaten hot.
steps: Toss the onion with the salt and leave for 10 minutes so it softens and releases juice.
Mix in the besan, cumin, turmeric and chilli, adding the water a splash at a time until the batter just coats the onion.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles straight away.
Fry heaped tablespoons for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, in 3 batches, draining on paper towel.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve hot.

recipes.title: Salmon Onigiri
recipes.summary: Hand-pressed Japanese rice triangles with a flaked salmon centre wrapped in nori, ideal for the lunchbox.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then simmer covered with the water for 15 minutes until tender, and rest covered for 10 minutes.
Pan-cook the salmon for 4 minutes each side until opaque and flakes easily, then flake it with the soy sauce.
Wet your hands, rub with a little salt, and press a quarter of the rice into a flat cup in your palm.
Add a spoonful of salmon, cover with more rice and press into a firm triangle. Make 8 onigiri.
Roll in the sesame seeds and wrap each with a strip of nori just before eating.
notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque all through, and keep onigiri in the fridge and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Pork and Cabbage Spring Rolls
recipes.summary: Crisp baked rolls filled with juicy pork mince, cabbage and ginger, served with a sharp vinegar dip.
steps: Stir-fry the pork in a hot pan for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches at least 75°C.
Add the cabbage, carrot and ginger and cook for 3 minutes until wilted, then stir in half the soy sauce and the sesame oil. Cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Spoon 3 tbsp of filling onto each wrapper, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing with a little water.
Brush with the neutral oil and bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the rice vinegar and serve alongside.
notes: Food safety: cook pork mince to at least 75°C; cool leftovers within 1 hour and refrigerate.

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Croquetas
recipes.summary: Creamy bechamel croquetas with ham and cheddar and a crisp crumb, a Spanish bar classic.
steps: Melt the butter, stir in 1/4 cup of the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk and stir for 8 minutes until very thick.
Fold in the ham, cheddar and nutmeg, then chill in a shallow dish for at least 2 hours until firm.
Shape into 18 small logs using wet hands. Roll in the remaining flour, the beaten eggs, then the breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the oil in batches over medium heat for 2 minutes, turning, until deep golden and hot through the middle.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg and keep the chilled mix refrigerated; eat leftovers within 2 days.

recipes.title: Potato Aloo Tikki
recipes.summary: Spiced potato patties with a crisp golden crust, served with yoghurt and chutney.
steps: Boil the potato whole for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then peel, mash and cool for 10 minutes.
Mix with the peas, spices, cornflour and salt.
Shape into 8 patties about 1.5cm thick.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until a crisp golden crust forms.
Serve hot with the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon if you like.

recipes.title: Lamb and Mint Sausage Rolls
recipes.summary: Flaky sausage rolls with spiced lamb mince and fresh mint, cut into party-size pieces.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Mix the lamb, onion, breadcrumbs, mint, cumin and salt.
Cut the pastry sheets in half, run a log of filling down each and roll up, sealing the join underneath.
Brush with the beaten egg, scatter with sesame seeds and cut each log into 4 pieces to make 24.
Bake on lined trays for 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and puffed.
Check the middle of one roll reads at least 75°C before serving.
notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach at least 75°C all through; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Prawn Toast Fingers
recipes.summary: Crisp sesame-topped toast spread with a prawn and ginger paste, pan-fried until golden.
steps: Blitz the prawns, egg white, ginger, cornflour and soy sauce into a rough paste.
Cut each slice of bread into 3 fingers and spread the paste thickly over one side. Press the sesame seeds on top.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry paste-side down for 2 minutes until golden.
Turn and fry for 2 minutes more until the bread is crisp and the prawn reads at least 63°C.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and at least 63°C; keep raw seafood refrigerated and cook within a day.

recipes.title: Masala Vada
recipes.summary: Crunchy South Indian lentil fritters with onion, chilli and fennel.

items: 1 cup split chickpeas (chana dal), soaked for 4 hours

steps: Drain the dal and blitz half of it to a coarse paste, leaving the rest whole for crunch.
Mix with the onion, chilli, fennel, coriander and salt.
Shape into 12 flat patties.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, draining on paper towel.
Serve warm, with chutney or yoghurt on the side, within 20 minutes of frying while the crust is crisp.

recipes.title: Baked Lamb Kibbeh Bites
recipes.summary: Torpedo-shaped bulgur shells with a spiced lamb and pine nut filling, baked until crisp outside.
steps: Soak the bulgur in cold water for 15 minutes, drain and squeeze dry. Knead with the first lamb, grated onion, allspice and salt, or blitz in a processor, until a smooth paste forms.
Fry the chopped onion in 1 tbsp of the oil for 4 minutes, add the filling lamb and cook for 6 minutes until no pink remains. Stir in the pine nuts and cinnamon and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). With wet hands, flatten a golf-ball of shell mix, fill, and close into a torpedo. Make 18.
Brush with the remaining oil and bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until browned and at least 75°C in the middle.
Serve warm with the yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach at least 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Potato Knish
recipes.summary: Baked pastry parcels of soft potato and caramelised onion, an Eastern European deli favourite.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, 1/4 cup of the oil, water and half the salt into a dough, kneading for 3 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potato for 12 minutes until tender, drain and mash. Cook the onion with the butter and remaining oil for 15 minutes until deep golden, then mix in the potato, pepper and remaining salt.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle and spoon the filling in a log along the long side.
Roll up, cut into 6 pieces and pinch the cut ends closed, standing them upright. Brush with the egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.
notes: Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Khaman Dhokla
recipes.summary: Light, spongy steamed chickpea-flour squares tempered with mustard seeds and sesame.
steps: Whisk the besan, semolina, sugar, turmeric, salt, water and lemon juice into a smooth batter.
Stir in the bicarbonate of soda until it froths, and pour at once into a greased 18cm tin.
Steam over boiling water, covered, for 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is springy.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds for 30 seconds, add the sesame seeds and pour over the dhokla.
Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 12 squares.

recipes.title: Baked Cinnamon Churros
recipes.summary: Ridged choux sticks baked until crisp, rolled in cinnamon sugar and served with melted chocolate.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Bring the water, butter, 1 tbsp sugar and salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until a smooth ball forms.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12cm lengths onto a lined tray with a star nozzle and bake for 20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Toss in the cinnamon and the remaining sugar while still warm.
Melt the chocolate with the milk and serve for dipping.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 churros with chocolate.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

recipes.title: Classic Lamingtons
recipes.summary: Squares of light sponge dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla.
Fold in the flour and first measure of milk until just combined and spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool fully, ideally overnight in an airtight container, then cut into 12 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa, then stir with the second measure of milk and the 1 tbsp butter over low heat until smooth and runny.
Dip each square in the icing, let the excess drip off and roll in coconut. Set for 30 minutes.
notes: Plus overnight cooling and 30 minutes setting.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg; the cake is baked until a skewer is clean.

recipes.title: Honey Walnut Baklava
recipes.summary: Crisp filo layers filled with spiced walnuts and soaked in lemon honey syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Mix the walnuts with the cinnamon.
Brush a 20cm square tin with butter and layer 6 filo sheets, brushing each with butter and trimming to fit.
Spread over the walnuts, then top with the remaining 6 sheets, brushing each with butter. Cut into 16 diamonds right through.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Simmer the honey, water and lemon juice for 8 minutes until slightly thick, pour over the hot baklava and cool for 3 hours.

recipes.title: Caramel Slice
recipes.summary: Three layers of shortbread base, soft condensed milk caramel and dark chocolate.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Mix the flour, coconut, sugar and melted butter, press into a lined 20cm square tin and bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir the condensed milk, 60g butter and golden syrup over medium heat for 10 minutes until thick and golden, constantly stirring.
Pour over the base and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with the oil and spread over the caramel. Chill for 2 hours.
Cut into 16 small squares with a hot knife and keep refrigerated.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Sultana Balls
recipes.summary: No-bake bites of sultanas, oats and peanut butter, rolled in coconut.
steps: Soak the sultanas in hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Blitz the sultanas, oats, peanut butter and honey into a sticky crumb that holds when squeezed.
Roll the mixture into 18 balls, squeezing firmly until each holds its shape.
Roll in the coconut until evenly coated.
Chill for 20 minutes until firm, and keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.
